statement: Design a small version of Twitter. Users post tweets, follow and unfollow other users, and ask for a news feed: the 10 most recent tweets posted by the user or by anyone they currently follow, newest first.

The operations arrive as one string, operations, with commands separated by semicolons: "post U T" (user U posts tweet T), "follow U V" (U starts following V), "unfollow U V" (U stops following V) and "feed U" (return U's news feed). Run them in order. A tweet's recency is the order in which it was posted.
A feed is built by merging the users' tweet lists, each newest first, with a max-heap keyed on posting time, and stopping after 10 tweets.
Return, for every user who asked for a feed, the feed from their last feed request, written as {user=[tweet ids, newest first], …}.

examples.explanation: User 1's first feed, while following user 2, is [202, 201, 101]. After unfollowing, user 2's tweets drop out, so the last feed user 1 asks for is just [101].
User 1's last feed comes after unfollowing user 2, so it holds only tweets from users 1 and 3, newest first: 32, 31, 11. User 2 follows nobody and sees only their own tweets, 22 and 21.
